explanation: Fires only on a '0' token inside a long run of repeated zeros (e.g. '0000000000[[0]]5313', '0000[[0]]00'); essentially silent (~2%) on everything else, including ordinary word-piece tokens.

Diffuse: fires strongly on a token right after an operator or label that is about to be followed by a number or argument (a space after '=' or 'of' in math word problems, 'Issue[[ ]]10', 'No[[.]]', 'radius:[[ ]]4px', reporter citations), but also on assorted function words and verbs in prose and code ('Written[[ by]]', 'if[[ age]]', 'who[[ releases]]'). No single clear rule.

Fires most strongly on a token that breaks or continues a long run of repeated characters (' +' after a run of zeros as in '000000000 +0800', a comma in '8888, 999', a chunk of repeated ';;;'). Weak (~20%) and scattered firing on mid-word subword pieces of names and technical terms.

Sports and game text, especially athlete stats and player descriptions: fires on tokens inside stat lines and position phrases ('GAA[[ =]]', '.53[[5]] winning percentage', 'as a[[ left]] back', 'power[[-play]]', 'led the CBA[[ in]] rebounding'). Weaker on video-game genre descriptions; near zero outside sports and games.

Fires on a word that completes a common prepositional or adverbial phrase about context or reference: mainly 'this' after 'in' or 'like' ('in[[ this]] site', 'like[[ this]]'), plus 'as[[ well]]', 'a decade[[ ago]]', 'wasn't[[ sure]]', 'let[[ me]]'. Fires weaker on other determiners and pronouns.

Fires on cognition verbs, mainly 'know', 'knew' and 'understand' (also 'thought'), especially in first- or second-person framings ('I don't know', 'You know', 'As we all know', 'I don't understand'). Also fires on the punctuation that opens a reported thought ('I thought[[:]]'). Weaker on speech verbs like 'said'.

Fires on long runs of whitespace used for column alignment, especially padding before a trailing comment marker or before a right-column field in court captions and license boxes. Weaker on some code tokens ('export default', 'window.setTimeout').

Fires on the field or domain noun in a 'type of profession or sport' phrase, mostly sport names ('football'/'footballer', 'soccer', 'ice hockey', 'Fútbol') and 'real estate', also 'beekeeping'. Weaker on other occupational fields ('investment banker', 'acting', 'botanist', 'Aviation').

Polysemantic. Fires on medical and anatomical word pieces ('myocard'-ial, 'diaphrag'-m, 'sacro'-iliitis, 'lum'-inal), on 'of' in sentence-initial 'One of', on code string literals and template parameters ('"class"', '"dd/MM/yyyy"', 'T3'), and on assorted other tokens.

Mainly fires on byte-fragment tokens of multi-byte non-ASCII characters (CJK, accented Slavic or Esperanto letters, Greek, emoji), shown as '�'. Also fires moderately on unrelated tokens (' in' in 'second in Kansas City', ' San' Diego, ' Pascal', math symbols).

Fires on the period or comma that ends a clause right after a place name, abbreviation, time, or quantity ('N.J[[.]]', 'p.m[[.]]', '30 min[[.]]', 'U.S[[.]]', 'Cumbria, England[[,]]', '1890[[,]]'), especially when it closes a factual detail before new information. Ordinary sentence-final periods fire weaker.

Fires on tokens inside code identifiers and syntax: generic or template parameters ('T1', '<T'), format specifiers ('%d'), digits in identifiers or years, separators ('=\'', ',"', '|'). Also fires on scattered prose tokens ('In the event', 'be able'). Mostly a code-structure detector with noise.

No clear pattern. Fires on mid-name and mid-term subword pieces ('Sk'-ins, 'Burn'-el, 'L'Ch'-aim, 'DDI', 'SEC'-JDA), on code keys ('class', 'options', '.responseText'), and on technical nouns ('motor', 'ring', 'near').

Mixed. Fires on 'E' in 'Vitamin E', 'LH', 'antioxidant', 'IS' in 'AS IS', and acronym pieces ('SRAM', 'SAT', 'NFV'). Also fires on unrelated prose tokens ('carries herself', 'time of year', 'proportional to', 'cross validation').
